terms: thirty to one hundred and fifty
ledgerSearch.outcome: CTD-0036 is decisive. The corpus alternates among thirty to one hundred and fifty, approximately one hundred and fifty, approximately five hundred, and nested subgroups, and the item requires the direct-trust threshold, the governance unit, and the full Scale population to be defined separately with the evidence and uncertainty behind each range. The shipped provisional framing is kept verbatim and the baseline's converges on a range is bounded by it. CTD-0076 requires the singular Scale, which is used in the restored nesting sentence.

findings.summary: The constitutional standing of the first community was replaced by a list of what it needs.

evidence.baseline: The first community is not a startup and it is not a movement. It is a founding community in the constitutional sense, the community whose experience of living inside the architecture will shape the architecture for everyone who comes after. This gives the first community a responsibility that subsequent communities will not have.
evidence.shipped: The first community would shape the architecture for those that follow. It therefore needs an explicit learning mandate, informed consent to the experimental character of the work, and a way to publish failures without turning residents into exhibits.

findings.authorizedBy: Compression, and catalog 4.3 applied to the opening denial.
findings.diagnosis: Not a startup and not a movement are the two things every reader will assume it is, so the retention limb applies. The clause that subsequent communities will be able to relax because the first community did the work is the gift the chapter is describing, and it is the reason the demand on the first community is fair. The shipped requirements are good and are kept; they answer a different question, which is what the community is owed rather than what it is.

findings.summary: The size argument lost its reasoning and kept only its number.

evidence.baseline: the first community must be large enough to test the relational architecture genuinely, and small enough that everyone in it can know everyone else. Volume III's analysis of group fields ... establishes that there is a scale threshold above which direct interpersonal trust gives way to institutional trust.
evidence.shipped: the first cohort must be large enough to expose the relational design and small enough for direct acquaintance to remain plausible. This manuscript uses thirty to one hundred and fifty people as a provisional range for a direct-trust group.

findings.diagnosis: CTD-0036 requires the direct-trust threshold and the full Scale population to be separate concepts with their evidence and uncertainty stated. The shipped text does that well and the restoration keeps it verbatim. What the paydown also removed was the reason the threshold exists, the shift from interpersonal to institutional trust, which is the mechanism the whole nesting proposal in Chapter Three depends on. Mechanism and number are separable, and only the number was in dispute.

findings.summary: Credit, running the other way. The kept governance and economics sentences are the prior pass's, and they supply tests the baseline asserts without providing.

evidence.baseline: It means the economic architecture must be visible and real enough that its actual qualities can be assessed rather than assumed. (The paragraph ends there; no test of visibility is given, and the governance paragraph names no minimum content for the rules.)
evidence.shipped: Those rules must include dissent, appeal, succession, amendment, and exit, and their legal and democratic adequacy still requires review. ... Subsidy should be visible rather than disguised as self-sufficiency. Participants need to know who provides capital, what influence follows it, which costs the community can meet, and which costs remain externalized.

findings.authorizedBy: R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT, recorded in the twenty-rule audit of 2026-07-31. The original record kept both with the note that they are more specific than the baseline and displace nothing.
findings.diagnosis: The baseline requires a genuine economic relationship and constitutional operation but names no check a founder could fail. The kept sentences convert both requirements into verifiable content: five named rule categories with review still owed, and a four-part disclosure test for subsidy. That is repair of the requirements' emptiness, not bounding of their scope, and under the ratified rule it is recorded as a finding in the prior pass's favor.

debtImpact.note: The provisional range framing, the refusal to establish a universal human threshold, and the nested-group requirement for a larger Scale are all kept against the baseline's convergence language.
Scale is used as the singular in the restored nesting sentence.

generations.title: Derived from the immutable baseline under the thirteen rules

reasoning.note: R-LEDGER-WINS. CTD-0036 governs the number and the shipped provisional language survives against the baseline's convergence claim. The mechanism behind the number is restored, because the item disputes the figure and not the reason for it.
R-PUNCT-STRUCT. Four em dashes. Three were parenthetical appositives and became comma pairs. One introduced a specification at the founding period and became a colon.

The shipped economics paragraph on visible subsidy and the shipped governance requirements of dissent, appeal, succession, amendment, and exit. Both are more specific than the baseline and neither displaces it.
The constitutional standing of the first community, the relational trust mechanism behind the size threshold, the anti-capture requirement and its reason, and the local adaptation paragraph.

openQuestions: The restored sentence that the founding period is the period of maximum founder influence and minimum distributed participation is a general empirical claim without a source. CTD-0078 governs sourcing for this volume. Restored and flagged.

The volume-04 voice card was prepared by the same pass that produced the shipped text, and its exemplar anchors and protected lines quote that text rather than the baseline. The card records `Author approved: pending tone, strategy, heading, and overcompression review`. The restoration keeps every line the card protects and otherwise follows the baseline, which means card and source now diverge in wording the card does not name. R-VOICE-BIND requires that the disagreement be raised rather than settled here: the card should be re-derived from whichever text the author approves.

Structural labels were frozen for this pass and none was touched. Every markdown heading, every standalone bold display line, every chapter label, and every all-capital display line is byte identical to its pre-edit state, in the same order, with the same blank-line separators on both sides. A label determines a section id, a section id is a public route, and `publishing/continuity/section-lineage.json` already records this volume's renames and resolves the historical routes. Changing one is a continuity decision and not an editorial one. Only the running prose between labels was restored. Where a baseline label names its section better than the current one, the cost is recorded here and the label is left alone.

regenerationTest.purpose: The rules must reproduce the section from the baseline without consulting the shipped text.
regenerationTest.method: Derived from the immutable baseline applying editorial/method/standard.md, the corpus voice card, the volume-04 voice card, and the debt ledger under R-LEDGER-WINS.
regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required. The section is the volume's best illustration that a ledger item can dispute a number while leaving the mechanism behind the number untouched, and that a pass which deletes both has paid down more than the item asked for.

audits.auditor: editorial-agent, generation 1 of the twenty-rule re-render lane
audits.scope: Full re-read of the current section against the immutable baseline under all twenty rules. The original record was derived under the thirteen-rule index; this audit adds the substitution count and the later rules: R-LEDGER-WINS-COROLLARY, R-CORRECTION-SCOPE, R-CANON-DELETION-RECORD, R-PAIRED-DELETION, R-CAUTIOUS-HALF, R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT, and R-REFRAIN-COST.

substitutionTest.rule: R-CAUTIOUS-HALF, substitution form, run as standing procedure before any pairing test
substitutionTest.method: Normalize both texts, strip markup, split into sentences of three or more words, count baseline sentences appearing verbatim in the current section.
substitutionTest.note: Well above zero, so the section is a restoration, not a substitution, and the pairing test applies. Verbatim survival understates fidelity here: every R-PUNCT-STRUCT repair and recorded bounding changes the sentence it lands in, so the non-surviving remainder was read against the diff and attributed rather than assumed lost.

audits.checked: R-CORRECTION-SCOPE: the CTD-0036 bounding lands exactly on the range claim it names, converting the baseline's convergence into a provisional working figure and adding the nesting requirement, with the restored trust mechanism before it untouched; verified at width. R-LEDGER-WINS-COROLLARY: the baseline was searched for the bounding language before accepting it as seeded; it contains none, so the seeded provenance recorded by the original pass is correct. R-CAUTIOUS-HALF: the size paragraph keeps both the committing threshold argument and the hedging provisional frame, which is the right order of survival, mechanism first, bound second. R-PAIRED-DELETION: thirty to one hundred and fifty, direct trust, and nested groups were swept forward; the same distinctions recur in The Relational Coherence Threshold and The First Scale, and all three ends now carry the same provisional framing, so no end dangles. R-TENSE, R-DEIXIS, R-NEGATION-STACK: nothing fires. R-REFRAIN-COST: the four On headers are parallel enumeration under 4.4's retention limb, recorded.
audits.conclusion: The restoration holds under the full twenty-rule index. Fourteen of eighteen baseline sentences survive verbatim; the remainder trace to four recorded punctuation repairs and the documented CTD-0036 bounding. One substitution credit recorded as F3. No prose change required.
